discussion.p: The intent is for `make_signed` and `make_unsigned` to reject `bool`, which is enforced by their Mandates element. However, enumerations whose underlying type is `bool` are accepted (presumably by accident), with implementation divergence:

tr.td:
If `T` is a (possibly cv-qualified) signed integer type () then the
member typedef type denotes `T`; otherwise, if `T` is a (possibly
cv-qualified) unsigned integer type then type denotes the
corresponding signed integer type, with the same cv-qualifiers as `T`;
otherwise, type denotes the signed integer type with smallest
rank () for which `sizeof(T) == sizeof(type)`, with the same
cv-qualifiers as `T`.
Mandates: `T` is an integral or enumeration type other than cv `bool`
or enumeration type whose underlying type is not `bool`.

If `T` is a (possibly cv-qualified) unsigned integer type () then the
member typedef type denotes `T`; otherwise, if `T` is a (possibly
cv-qualified) signed integer type then type denotes the corresponding
unsigned integer type, with the same cv-qualifiers as `T`; otherwise,
type denotes the unsigned integer type with smallest rank () for
which `sizeof(T) == sizeof(type)`, with the same cv-qualifiers as
`T`.
Mandates: `T` is an integral or enumeration type other than cv `bool`
or enumeration type whose underlying type is not `bool`.
